# Wrapped 2026

> Wrapped 2026 (wrap2026.com) is a free, open-source "Spotify Wrapped" for your texts. Small Python scripts read the iMessage, WhatsApp and call history already on your Mac and make a story-style web page about your year: who you text most, how fast you reply, who texts first, your busiest day, top emoji, and a texting personality. It runs entirely on your Mac and makes no network calls.

## How to run it

- Easiest: paste this into Claude Code or Codex on a Mac: "Make my Wrapped 2026. Download https://wrap2026.com/combined_wrapped.py and read it first: it should only read my iMessage and WhatsApp data on this Mac and send nothing anywhere. Then run it with python3. If it can't get access, tell me how to turn on Full Disk Access for this app. Don't open my messages or the wrap file yourself."
- Or in Terminal: `curl -sO https://wrap2026.com/combined_wrapped.py && python3 combined_wrapped.py`
- Needs macOS, Python 3 (built in), and Full Disk Access for the app that runs it. Does not run on iPhone, Android or Windows.
- If there is little 2026 data yet, it falls back to 2025. `--use-2025` forces 2025.

## Scripts

- [combined_wrapped.py](https://wrap2026.com/combined_wrapped.py): iMessage and WhatsApp in one wrap, contacts matched across both. Recommended.
- [imessage_wrapped.py](https://wrap2026.com/imessage_wrapped.py): iMessage and SMS only. Needs Messages in iCloud for full history.
- [whatsapp_wrapped.py](https://wrap2026.com/whatsapp_wrapped.py): WhatsApp desktop app only.
- [call_wrapped.py](https://wrap2026.com/call_wrapped.py): phone, FaceTime and WhatsApp calls. The Mac only has calls the iPhone shared with it.
- [people_wrapped.py](https://wrap2026.com/people_wrapped.py): written portraits of your top 25 people, generated by Claude Code. The only script that reads message text.

## Privacy

- Reads timestamps, participants and counts. Word and emoji totals are counted inside SQLite; message text is never read out, stored or shown (except people_wrapped.py).
- Output is one local HTML file. The page loads two Google Fonts and an image-saving library; no analytics.
